dean.name: Dr. Soud Alli Tengah, PsyD
dean.role: Acting Dean of Students | Clinical Psychologist | Mental Health Researcher
dean.portrait_alt: Portrait of Dr. Soud Alli Tengah, PsyD, Acting Dean of Students
dean.summary: Dr. Soud Alli Tengah, PsyD, is a licensed Clinical Psychologist, researcher, and mental health systems leader with over 12 years of experience across East Africa.
biography: Dr. Soud Alli Tengah is a licensed Clinical Psychologist, researcher, and mental health systems leader with over 12 years of experience in clinical practice, research, training, and programme development across East Africa.

He provides leadership in student welfare, mental health promotion, and counselling services at the Technical University of Mombasa (TUM), supporting a university community of more than 21,000 students and 800 staff members.

With expertise in clinical psychology and mental health systems development, Dr. Tengah champions accessible, inclusive, and evidence-based support services. His work encompasses mental health promotion, counselling, early intervention, crisis response, psychological assessment, and referral services.
He is also committed to strengthening professional development through mentorship, clinical supervision, internships, and collaboration with universities and mental health training institutions.

An accomplished researcher, Dr. Tengah has published in peer-reviewed journals covering adolescent and emerging adult mental health, depression, anxiety, substance use, stigma reduction, HIV programming, and health systems strengthening.

message_paragraphs: I believe that mental health and well-being are fundamental to academic excellence, personal growth, healthy relationships, and workplace productivity.

At the Technical University of Mombasa, our commitment is to foster an inclusive and supportive university community where every student and staff member feels valued, supported, and empowered to reach their full potential.

Through accessible student support services, effective counselling, mental health promotion, and collaborative partnerships, we strive to create an environment in which individuals can overcome challenges, flourish, and contribute meaningfully to society.

student_life.title: Student Association
student_life.short: Learn how TUMSA represents students, supports welfare and provides ways to participate in University life.
student_life.image_alt: TUMSA Comrades Project Alliance student banner
student_life.hero_intro: The Technical University of Mombasa Students Association (TUMSA) represents students, advocates for their welfare and provides a democratic channel for student participation.
about: TUMSA is the students’ representative association at the Technical University of Mombasa. Guided by its Constitution, it works to represent students’ rights, interests and aspirations and to provide a democratic way to raise concerns and contribute to University life.

The Association brings students together while respecting different backgrounds, cultures, beliefs and abilities. Its work is guided by transparency, accountability, participation, integrity and social justice.
student_life.participate: Connect with your School, Institute, hall or campus representative; attend student meetings and forums; participate in elections; and contribute to approved welfare, sports, entertainment and community-service activities. Consult the TUMSA Constitution through the University or TUMSA for details of membership and governance.

sections.title: Student representation
paragraphs: TUMSA’s constitutional structures provide ways for students to share concerns and participate in decisions affecting student life.
points: The Student Council carries out leadership and day-to-day functions assigned by the Constitution and engages with relevant University offices on student affairs and welfare.
The TUMSA Congress is the Association’s supreme policy-making organ under the Constitution, bringing student representatives together for deliberation and policy decisions.

School and Institute representatives communicate students’ views and academic concerns. Other constituencies include halls of residence, satellite campuses, students with special needs and religious groups, as provided for in the Constitution.

sections.title: Student welfare
paragraphs: TUMSA liaises with relevant University departments and offices on matters affecting students’ everyday welfare.
points: Accommodation and conditions in halls of residence and outside hostels.
Catering and access to affordable meals.
Health, hygiene, clean water and access to health services.
Coordination when students experience sickness or bereavement.

sections.title: Inclusion and student activities
paragraphs: The Constitution provides for representation of students with special needs and promotes their integration into the University community. TUMSA can raise accessibility and inclusion concerns with the Association and appropriate University bodies.
TUMSA also supports student interaction through sports, tournaments, entertainment and approved activities. These provide opportunities for teamwork, talent development and community participation.
points: Encourage academic excellence, research, and the development of artistic and professional talents.
Promote freedom of expression, association, conscience and academic liberty within applicable laws and University regulations.
Build unity among students from different backgrounds and foster constructive relationships with University staff and the wider public.
Encourage community service and cooperation with TUM alumni.

sections.title: Elections and accountability
paragraphs: TUMSA leadership and representation are established through constitutional processes, including elections. The Constitution provides for a University Electoral Commission to oversee specified student elections and procedures.

This page is an accessible overview based on the TUMSA Constitution (April 2020), not a replacement for the Constitution. Refer to the Constitution through the University or TUMSA for complete information on membership, rights, responsibilities and governance.

about: The TUM Mental Health and Well-Being Centre promotes holistic psychological wellbeing across the University community. Its work includes prevention, early intervention, counselling, crisis response, education, research and community engagement.
The Centre provides confidential, professional and compassionate support. Reaching out for help is a sign of strength, and you do not need to wait until things become overwhelming.
student_services.access: Book a virtual or in-person session through the TUM Mental Health and Well-Being Centre website. For support by phone or email, use the contact details on this page.

student_services.title: Hostels & Accommodation
student_services.short: Comfortable hostels and help finding off-campus housing near the University.
student_services.image_alt: Uhuru Hostel at the Technical University of Mombasa
student_services.hero_intro: Find safe, affordable and student-friendly accommodation while you pursue your academic goals.
about: The Accommodation Section provides clean, safe and student-friendly hostel accommodation to support students during their studies. On-campus bed spaces are limited, and the University also assists students to identify private hostels near campus.
Priority consideration for on-campus accommodation is given to students with special needs and international students, in consultation with the Office of the Dean of Students.
student_services.access: Reserve a bed through the University's Online Room Reservation Portal. After a successful reservation, pay the accommodation fee through the e-Citizen platform. For private hostel options near the University, contact the Accommodation Section for assistance.
student_services.location: Accommodation Office: near the Dining Hall. Janitors' Office: next to the Health Unit and Block SE (Umoja), Ground Floor.
student_services.hours: Resident students are supported day and night. During official working hours, visit the Accommodation Office. After hours, hostel Janitors supervise the hostels and attend to urgent matters and student grievances, including weekends and public holidays.

accommodation_details.vision: To become a model accommodation services unit among institutions of higher learning in Kenya.
accommodation_details.mission: To provide high-quality, affordable and reasonably priced accommodation to students and visiting groups.
services: Maintaining cleanliness and hygiene in hostels and surrounding areas.
Helping students arrange private hostel accommodation.
Providing friendly, experienced and supportive accommodation staff.
Providing continuous hostel supervision to support a safe and conducive living environment.
accommodation_details.visitor_rate: KSh 350–500 per person per night during holiday breaks.
accommodation_details.cooking_notice: Cooking is strictly prohibited in the hostels.
accommodation_details.cafeteria: A cafeteria is available within the University compound, offering meals on a pay-as-you-eat basis.

student_services.title: Health Unit
student_services.short: On-campus primary healthcare and wellness support.
student_services.image_alt: Exterior of the TUM Health Unit building
student_services.hero_intro: Primary healthcare, clinical services and wellness support for the TUM community.
about: The Technical University of Mombasa Health Centre is a registered Level 2 medical facility serving the University community. From its beginnings as a small dispensary, it has grown to a team of approximately 10 healthcare professionals, with a strategic objective to transition to a Level 3 hospital by 2028.
The Health Services Department provides primary care to eligible students, staff and covered dependants at the Main Campus in Mombasa and through a satellite clinic at the Kwale Campus Extension.
student_services.access: Students attending for the first time should bring a valid TUM Student ID or proof of current-session registration, such as a fee statement or registration slip. Returning students should bring their TUM Hospital Card and Student ID. Students are expected to be registered with SHA/SHIF, directly or as a dependant. Staff and dependants are served under medical insurance covers accepted by the facility.
student_services.emergency_notice: For emergencies after 5:00 PM or on weekends, call the Health Centre In-Charge, Dr. Rerimoi, on 0721 848 952. You can also contact the TUM Security Officer on duty, who will alert the healthcare provider on call. For life-threatening emergencies, seek emergency assistance immediately.
student_services.location: Main Campus, Mombasa; and the satellite clinic at the Kwale Campus Extension.
student_services.hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. Closed weekends and public holidays.

health_details.facility_level: Registered Level 2 medical facility, with a strategic objective to transition to Level 3 by 2028.
eligibility: Registered TUM students currently in session.
student_requirements: First visit: valid TUM Student ID, or proof of current-session registration such as a fee statement or registration slip.
Revisit: TUM Hospital Card issued at the first visit and Student ID.
Students are expected to be registered under SHA/SHIF, either directly or as dependants under a parent or guardian.
services: Triage and nursing care, including preliminary vital signs, temperature and blood-pressure checks.
Outpatient consultation, diagnosis and treatment by Clinical Officers and Clinical Assistants.
Consultations with a visiting Gynecological Consultant.
Registered pharmacy services; if a medicine is out of stock, an official prescription is provided for external purchase.
Basic diagnostic investigations and clinical laboratory tests.
Wound dressing and minor procedures for minor trauma, burns and surgical dressings.
TB screening, monitoring and treatment referral.
Voluntary, confidential HIV Testing and Counselling Services (HTS), including pre- and post-test counselling and wellness guidance.
workflow: Pharmacy, laboratory or HTS service as needed
Discharge or referral to a Level 3 or 4 facility
referral_hospitals: Nearby Level 3 or 4 facilities near the student's residence
health_details.service_limit: Maternal, antenatal and delivery services are not offered on-site. Referrals are issued for specialized reproductive health services.
